name: 409 Juvenile Mentorship Program
description: SECTION ONE: The purpose of 409 Juvenile Mentorship Program is to serve as an outlet for Emory students to provide academic support for youth in detention centers. description: The mission of AAPI@Candler is to create a space where the experiences and insights of Asian, Asian-American, and Pacific Islander students can flourish, both within the community and in the broader Candler context. Through fostering meaningful connections and cultural exchange, the group supports students who identify as AAPI or who seek to learn more about AAPI cultures. AAPI@Candler is committed to enriching the Candler community by cultivating belonging and empowering AAPI students in their academic, spiritual, and communal journeys.

The goal of these clinics is to use the game of tennis to foster the enjoyment of fitness, improve gross and small-motor skills, hand-eye coordination, communications, social skills, and self-esteem of children with autism.

name: Active Minds
description: Championing a New Era of Mental Health We envision a society that forever values and prioritizes mental health. By equipping, connecting, and amplifying the collective and diverse voices of youth and young adults, we are building a movement of lasting champions who are improving mental health norms for all.

Being a part of Adrenaline provides students the opportunity to develop their dance skills, choreograph new routines, make friends and learn about the Emory hip-hop community.

name: AdventureATL

name: African Caribbean Student Union
description: The African Caribbean Student Union at Oxford College of Emory University is dedicated to fostering a vibrant, inclusive, and supportive community for students of African and Caribbean heritage, as well as allies interested in learning about these cultures. Our mission is to celebrate and uplift the diverse traditions, histories, and identities of Africa and the Caribbean through cultural programming, dialogue, service, and advocacy. name: Afro-Latinx Student Association
description: The purpose of the Afro-Latinx Student Association is to build and foster a community of Afro-Latinx-identifying students at Emory University. There has not been a space on campus that caters to the unique identity and experience of being Afro-Latinx. We aim to share knowledge about the complexities and intersectionality of being Black and Latinx within our community but also with the Emory community at large. We aim to share our music, dance, history, traditions, and anything else that makes our experiences and culture unique.

description: As a team, Emory Agnition’s strives to understand the significance behind different modern and traditional Indian dance forms, such as Bollywood, Bharatanatyam, Bhangra, Hip Hop, and Kuthu; choreograph and perform fusion dance pieces at Emory events and inter-collegiate level competitions; enrich the community with Bollywood dance styles through performance pieces.

name: AHANA A Cappella
description: AHANA A Cappella is Emory's Multicultural, RnB-focused A Cappella Group. Originally founded by Will Corbin and Jasmine McGinnis, AHANA has been performing around campus for over 20 years, most recently performing at our NPR Tiny Desk-inspired concert in collaboration with Emory Campus Life and at the Masters of Finance Graduation Ceremony. AHANA is known for it's great sound, style, and the energy we bring to every performance. Keep an eye out for us!

name: Aikido Club
description: The mission of the Emory Aikido Club is to provide a welcoming community for Emory University students, faculty, and staff, promote health and wellness through physical activity, teach self-defense skills, and offer opportunities to practice the martial art of Aikido to members of all skill levels.

name: All Black Emory
description: All Black Emory exists to foster a dynamic space for dialogue, connection, and truth-telling among Black members of the Emory community. The AHC is dedicated to representing student interests, establishing monetary policy, and overseeing expenditures, while also fostering communication among students, faculty, and administration within Allied Health.

APCO partners with The Aflac Cancer Center at CHOA, in the top 10 childhood cancer centers and one of the largest clinical trial programs in the country, and the Atlanta Ronald McDonald House Charities to provide both financial and emotional support for the families of children battling cancer.

The group tends to steer away from customary “doo-wop” arrangements and instead prides itself on passionate energy and modern style. Aural Pleasure strives to foster a musically innovative environment and encourages its members to toy with unconventional sound and push the boundaries of traditional a cappella. description: The purpose of the Emory Badminton Association is to provide a weekly opportunity for individuals to participate in the sport of badminton at both a recreational and competitive level. Good sportsmanship, fostering connections among persons of all nationalities and experience levels, and the provision of an opportunity to foster physical fitness are goals of the Association.

We focus on educating members on the technique and culture associated with various styles of ballroom dance. We compete around the US at varsity competitions and our performance group performs at various Emory events. Recently, we've partnered with the American Cancer Society Hope Lodge to provide free lessons every month to their residents and their visitors.

description: The mission of Beta Alpha Psi at Emory University is to create a supportive and inclusive community for students pursuing accounting and related fields. We aim to connect students with valuable resources, foster meaningful relationships with peers and professionals, and provide opportunities for personal and professional growth—so that no student in this path feels alone in their journey.

name: Bike Social
description: The Emory Bike Social is a group of undergraduate students dedicated to promoting cycling in the Emory community. We organize regular group bike rides (usually with free food and great scenery!) as well as educational, environmentalism, sustainability, and activism-oriented events. We also collaborate with the Emory Spokes Council, our graduate student club, to run the Fixie, a vibrant bike co-op (free bike repair shop) on campus.

name: Center for Civic & Community Engagement
description: Emory's Center for Civic and Community Engagement (CCE) supports members of the Emory community to develop and apply their skills to foster a kinder and more socially just world. The Emory Ice Hockey Club aims to enrich the Atlanta hockey community by serving as Emory University’s official ice hockey club, increasing both student involvement in athletics and school spirit.

description: Dedicated to the histories, cultures, and political movements of black communities across the United States and wider African diaspora, African American Studies at Emory University pursues academic excellence and social responsibility through interdisciplinary scholarship, transformational pedagogy, and engagement with local, national, and international communities of African descent.

We hope to serve as a forum for both ecology-focused students and the broader Emory community to come together to appreciate our natural spaces and understand the challenges facing them.

description: EEVM’s mission is to spur intellectual growth and curiosity by creating a successful support system and community for students wishing to pursue entrepreneurship at Emory. We aim to lower barriers into entrepreneurship. description: The mission of Emory HOPE is to serve as an outlet for students to engage in and learn from rewarding experiences unique to hospice work. For students interested in healthcare careers, Emory HOPE will be especially helpful in exposing these students to palliative care, an often-overseen side of healthcare, and the ethical issues surrounding end-of-life care and patient advocacy. The main initiative of Emory HOPE shall be to connect student volunteers with hospice patients for long-term patient interaction and care.

name: Emory Hypertension Awareness Program
description: The Emory Hypertension Awareness Program (HAP) is a passionate student-led organization focused on raising awareness about hypertension and cardiovascular diseases, including heart attack and stroke. JMSA is open to all medical students, regardless of religion, nationality, or background.

description: The mission of Emory Music Business Club is to create a vibrant space for Emory students passionate about the music industry to collaborate, gain hands-on experience, and deepen their understanding of the music business. Additionally, the organization shall involve the student body and community in social events to encourage fun perspectives of the brain.

description: The purpose of Emory Science Olympiad is to increase accessibility and learning of scientific knowledge among K-12 students in the Atlanta area through increasing engagement with the Science Olympiad Organization at local schools. Through volunteering with local Newton County organizations, hosting culturally themed tournaments and soccer watch parties, and fundraising for causes like TOPSoccer and Special Olympics, we aim to foster inclusivity, promote community engagement, and share the unifying spirit of soccer with all.

The Society seeks both to promote an awareness of these principles and to further their application through its activities.

We are committed to amplifying FLI voices, creating lasting institutional change, and expanding access to resources that empower FLI students to thrive academically, socially, and professionally.

description: Two7 exists to equip students with the tools of fundamental investing, foster disciplined and independent thinking, and extend financial literacy to the broader community. Through education, discussion, and service, we train our members to approach investing with rigor, humility, and conviction.

description: Ubuntu Theater Group’s mission is to bring together a community of students of color in theater through collaboration and artistry.

name: Under One Moon Association
description: The Under One Moon Association aims to serve as a welcoming and open-minded community for all Oxford students regardless of race, ethnicity, gender identity, sexual orientation, religious affiliation, ability, or anything that makes one’s personal identity unconventional. Based on the final line of the Song Dynasty poem Water Melody and the title of the 2007 film Under the Same Moon, UOMA operates with the belief that everyone around the world is united by gazing up at the same moon every night.

name: Undergraduate Journal Club
description: The Emory Undergraduate Journal Club (EUJC) provides Emory undergraduate students with an opportunity to explore research, regardless of their major or areas of interest. The club aims to familiarize students with common research practices, involve them in self-driven research, and improve their skills in research presentation, all of which are crucial for Emory scholars to develop. Additionally, the Journal Club serves as a platform for networking and building meaningful connections with fellow researchers. description: The Undergraduate Nursing Council (UNC) is a constituent of the Georgia Association of Nursing Students and the National Student Nurses Association. name: Undergraduate Research Journal
description: The Emory Undergraduate Research Journal (EURJ) is intended to be the primary print outlet for research and scholarly work done by Emory undergraduates. EURJ is committed to the following objectives: maintaining high standards in Journal quality and professionalism; securing a blind review of manuscripts by expert reviewers; and delivering a thought-provoking publication that is accessible to a wide undergraduate audience.

name: United Nations International Children's Emergency Fund
description: To advance children’s rights and well-being globally by engaging the Emory community in education, advocacy, and service.

description: The purpose of United on Campus Club at Emory University shall be to provide a means for students at Emory University to support the mission of Blood Cancer United. Blood Cancer United believes everyone with blood cancer deserves a longer, better life. That’s why their mission is to cure blood cancer and improve the quality of life of all patients and their families. description: The mission of Universities Allied for Essential Medicines shall be to advocate for the development and expansion of new and existing drug therapies for people suffering from neglected diseases.

name: University Latin Club
description: To promote the study of classical cultures and to enhance the appreciation of the Latin language in higher education.

name: University MatheMatic Association (EUMMA)
description: We aim to provide an academic focused club for students planning to take the Math major (Math, AMS, Applied math, ect.). Students who are not math majors are also welcome to participate. We hope to organize events for students to learn more about the application of math in different areas, preparing them for future paths, such as joining research, looking for jobs, and applying for graduate programs. This platform is open for students to explore and connect with others who are also interested in math, creating an environment that fosters communication and creativity.

name: University School of Medicine Gun Violence Prevention Interest Group
description: The Emory University School of Medicine Gun Violence Prevention Interest Group is a nonpartisan student group dedicated to addressing the critical role of physicians in gun violence prevention through physician panels, educational lectures, clinical skill workshops, and community engagement. description: US4L is committed to fostering awareness, education, and engagement in longevity science and providing students with unparalleled opportunities to delve into this burgeoning field. Our efforts are concentrated on propelling progress and nurturing talent, accelerating advancements in longevity science. name: Uplifting Marginalized Mothers & Individuals
description: UMMI supports refugee and incarcerated women, along with others impacted by injustice. We focus on healing, community, and creating meaningful opportunities that help people move forward with strength and dignity.

name: Urology Interest Group
description: The Urology Interest Group (UIG) at Emory University School of Medicine provides medical students with early exposure to the exciting field of urology

name: UV&Me
description: The mission of the UV&Me Emory Chapter is to promote sun safety, skin health, and dermatologic awareness among diverse communities through education, outreach, and advocacy. We strive to empower students and the greater Atlanta community with knowledge about the importance of UV protection, skin cancer prevention, and healthy skin practices. By engaging in service, peer education, and collaboration with dermatology faculty and local organizations, we aim to reduce health disparities, foster inclusive dermatologic education, and inspire the next generation of leaders in skin health.

name: Value Investment Group
description: The Oxford Stocks Investment Club offers students the opportunity to gain experience in the stock market by examining successful companies and start-ups that might be the next Apple or Amazon. We want to create as many successful investors as possible and give them opportunities to join great venture capital firms. We will learn and master the strategies for investments in order to create financial wealth (freedom).

name: Vascular Surgery Interest Group
description: Emory Vascular Surgery Interest Group (EVSIG) aims to promote vascular-related activities to students at Emory SOM, provides students with early exposure to surgery, and assist students as they seek valuable career mentorship.

name: Vibez Dance Troupe
description: Vibez Dance Troupe is the first and only Caribbean dance team on Emory’s campus. We strive to highlight a multitude of Caribbean dance styles like soca, dance hall, kompa and dembow. In addition, our goals are to provide a pathway for Caribbean students and those interested in the culture to express themselves as well as spreading awareness across campus.

name: Vietnamese Student Association
description: Emory’s Vietnamese Student Association aims to spread Vietnamese culture and foster a sense of community between its members through our annual gala, social events, sports teams, and family group outings. We also develop leadership and networking skills by creating relationships with other Vietnamese Student Associations through collaboration and annual UVSASE events.

name: Visual Media Club
description: The Visual Media Club (VMC) aims to be an inclusive space for creators and enjoyers of all forms of visual storytelling (including but not limited to comics, manga, manhwa, animation, film, and video games). Through artistic expression, discussion, and shared appreciation, VMC seeks to explore styles and narratives across cultures while encouraging members to develop their own creative skills, exchange ideas, and connect with others with similar interests.

name: Voices of Inner Strength Gospel Choir
description: We are Voices of Inner Strength (VOIS) Gospel Choir: Emory University's gospel choir. We are dedicated to serving the Lord on campus and in the Atlanta community through singing and fellowship. We are always looking for new members who are moved to sing and serve Christ–no audition required!

name: Volunteer Emory
description: Volunteer Emory's mission is to collaborate with agents of change for service projects and social justice work that promote learning about self and society Overview of Programs: Volunteer Emory, operating out of the Center for Civic and Community Engagement, offers students the chance to engage in the community through weekly service trips, alternative breaks, Days of Service, and social justice education as well as Community Connection events.

name: Volunteer Medical Interpretation Services
description: VMIS is an organization that strives to promote medical literacy in underprivileged communities by providing voluntary medical interpretation services from its certified medical interpreters. Students seeking to dismantle language barriers between healthcare providers and patients with low English proficiency work to attain medical interpretation certification through VMIS and ALTA Language Services, Inc. name: Volunteer Oxford
description: Where service meets advocacy, social justice, and equity

name: Water: Advocacy: Voice: and Education
description: The mission of Waves Swimming Club is to promote water safety and confidence by educating Black and other communities of color on safe swimming practices. We aim to break down barriers, provide access to resources, and create an inclusive environment where everyone feels empowered to learn, enjoy, and thrive in aquatic spaces.

name: Wilderness Medical Society
description: To expose Emory medical students to the outdoors and teach them about Wilderness Medicine!

name: WMRE Emory Radio
description: WMRE is Emory's student-run radio station, where DJs can host weekly and biweekly one-hour shows. WMRE also releases the music and culture zine Frequency with content created entirely by Emory students and hosts community events centered around music and art. The station streams live 24/7 online at www.wmre.live. Turn us on!

name: Wok Boba Club
description: Wok Boba aims to build an inclusive community through exceptional service to others by the creation of delicious boba.

name: Wok Hey Oxford (Emory Oxford Cultural Cooking Club)
description: Preserve, celebrate, and promote the diverse cultural values, traditions, and stories of the Emory Oxford student and faculty body through the culinary lens by fostering an inclusive community where students can learn, connect, and build meaningful relationships through the shared experience of cooking and food.

name: Women in Business
description: Emory Women in Business is an undergraduate organization at Emory University created to facilitate personal and professional development of all current and past students associated with Emory.

name: Women in Law
description: The purpose of Emory Women in Law is to close the gap in existing clubs for a space exclusively for those identifying as women who are interested in law. Within this organization, we intend to address adversities and discrepancies that women face in law, in addition to fostering a community of like-minded individuals.

name: Women in Neuroscience
description: The purpose of this organization is to cultivate a community of graduate student researchers at Emory University that support the advancement of women in neuroscience. To accomplish this, our aim is two-fold: 1) we aim to support women-identified graduate level researchers interested in neuroscience at Emory University by hosting speakers, panel discussions, networking events, and social events, 2) we aim to cultivate a community that will assist our members throughout their time at Emory University and beyond, as they pursue their career aspirations. name: Women in Sports
description: Our mission is to foster unity, empowerment, and professional growth for women pursuing careers in sports and for all who support this community at Emory University. We are committed to building an inclusive environment where members can thrive academically, professionally, and personally while developing the skills and confidence needed to succeed in a competitive industry.

name: Women in STEM
description: Women in STEM serves as a safe forum and open mental space for all students who identify as a woman and study a STEM discipline. STEM is not limited to the "hard sciences" and we believe that developing an interdisciplinary dialogue between women in every field of study is essential to moving forward in today's world. We are a group of women who have joined together to create a community where we can voice our concerns, support each other in our passions, and empower other women to pursue and succeed in STEM careers.

name: Women's Club Basketball
description: We are Emory Women's Club Basketball! Our team members have a range of skill levels, but most played in high school (or longer). We work hard, but like to have fun while doing so. We practice regularly, scrimmage with local teams, and travel to compete in larger tournaments. Please reach out if you are interested in joining or would like to have any questions answered! name: Women's Club Soccer
description: The primary goal of the club is to bring soccer to a greater number of people in the undergraduate Emory community by providing a competitive soccer environment for women of the Emory community.

name: Year Zero Cinema Club
description: To encourage the cinephiles of Emory University in their passions, providing them a place to express their thoughts on the films they love, and a community in which to nurture their individual interests.

name: Young Democrats of Emory
description: The Young Democrats of Emory serves to civically engage the Emory student body by hosting discussion-based events, bringing speakers and local activists to the College, and working with other advocacy organizations on campus. Our goal is to create and promote activism throughout Emory and to extend that work into the Atlanta community and beyond. Additionally, we support the broader mission of the Democratic Party through our activism as we promote party values and candidates through our efforts. The work we have done has helped register thousands of students within the Emory community to vote

name: Young Emory Physicists
description: Foster community engagement among Physics graduate students and providing them a platform to interact socially and scientifically.

name: Zeebah
description: Zeebah’s mission is to provide students at Emory University a diverse, all-female dance group that performs a wide range of dances, including traditional belly dance, while blending traditional and modern styles to celebrate movement, culture, and creativity. We create a welcoming space for women to connect with their bodies, express themselves through dance, and build a strong, supportive community. The name Zeebah, meaning “beautiful” in Farsi, reflects our commitment to empowering one another through the shared joy of performance, self-expression, and sisterhood.
